title: About this task
paragraphs: Task 1.1 assesses user needs, mobility gaps, and potential demand for Rural Autonomous Vehicle (RAV) passenger transportation services in rural and tribal communities. It looks at both the people who would ride and the organizations that operate, manage, or coordinate rural mobility services.

University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee leads the task, with the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Georgia, and Oklahoma State University supporting. The work builds on UWM's senior mobility transportation needs survey for WisDOT, which covered more than 70 counties, 13 transit agencies, and 83 service providers.

tasks.title: 1. User needs and expectations study
tasks.text: Surveys, interviews, and focus groups with rural and tribal residents, caregivers, and service providers about travel needs, access barriers, and comfort with AV services.

tasks.title: 2. Stakeholder engagement
tasks.text: Working with advocacy and service organizations so that non-driver, older adult, disability, and rural mobility perspectives shape the study.

tasks.title: 3. Demand forecasting
tasks.text: Modeling potential demand for RAV services using the survey results, demographic trends, and economic and infrastructure conditions.
